label: Re=0,2
title: Proof
body_md:
We multiply the heat  equation \eqref{heat.eq} by $u$ and integrating on the group ${\mathbb{G}}$ and obtain the equality:
		\begin{equation*}\label{Re=0,2}
			\Re(\langle u_t(t,\cdot),u(t,\cdot)\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{G})}+\langle \mathcal{R}u(t,\cdot),u(t,\cdot)\rangle_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+\langle V(\cdot)u(t,\cdot),u(t,\cdot) \rangle_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})})=0\,,
		\end{equation*}
		for all $t \in [0,T]$. The last equality can be rewritten as
		\begin{equation}\label{prop2.any.sob}
		    \frac12	\partial_t\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}^2+\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}^2+\|\sqrt{V^{+}}u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}^2= \|\sqrt{V^{-}}u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^{2}({\mathbb{G}})}^2
		\end{equation}
		for all $t \in [0,T]$, where $V^+,V^-$ are the positive and negative parts of $V$, respectively.
		Straightforward computations yield 
		\[\|\sqrt{V^{-}}u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^{2}({\mathbb{G}})}\leq \|\sqrt{V^-}\|_{L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})}\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \leq \|\sqrt{|V|}\|_{L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})}\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,. \]
		Thus, equation \eqref{prop2.any.sob} implies for the time-derivative of $\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}$:
		\begin{equation}\label{before.G}	\frac12 \partial_t\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}^2 \leq \|\sqrt{|V|}\|_{L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})}^2 \|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}^2\,,
		\end{equation}
		for all $t \in [0,T]$.
	Hence we can apply Gr\"{o}nwall's inequality to \eqref{before.G}, so that 
	\[
	\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \leq \|u_0\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\exp \left(\int_{0}^{t}\|V\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb{G}})}\,ds \right)\,,
	\]
	and we obtain the desired estimate \eqref{prop.neg.a.claim}. This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop.neg.a}.
head: environment

label: rem.any.sob
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem.any.sob}
	Let us point out that, under the assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop.neg.a}, the solution $u\in L^2({\mathbb{G}})$ to the Cauchy problem \eqref{heat.eq}, belongs also to the Sobolev space of order $\frac{\nu}{2}$: Indeed, by \eqref{prop2.any.sob} we get 
	\[
\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{\dot{L}^{2}_{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})}=	\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}u(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2} \leq \|\sqrt{V^-}\|_{L^\infty}^2 \|u\|_{L^2}^{2}\,,
	\]
	with the right-hand side of the last inequality being, by the assumptions of Proposition \ref{prop.neg.a}, finite.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $X$ be a normed space of functions/distributions and let $\omega(\epsilon)$ be as in \eqref{mol}.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item   A net of functions/distributions $(f_\epsilon)_\epsilon \in X$ is said to be \textit{$X$-moderate} if there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that \[
		\|f_\epsilon\|_{X}\lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^{-N}\,,
		\]
		for all $\epsilon \in (0,1]$.
		\item A net of functions/distribitions $(u_\epsilon)_\epsilon=(u_\epsilon(t,\cdot))_\epsilon$ in $C([0,T]; X)$ is said to be \textit{$C([0,T]; X)$-moderate} if there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that 
		\[
		\sup_{t \in [0,T]}\|u_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{X}\lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^{-N}\,,
		\]
		for all $\epsilon \in (0,1]$.
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Moderateness

label: rem:e'
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:e'}
Trivially, for nets that arise as regularisations of a distribitional function in some normed space $X$ via a mollifier the $X$-moderate assumption is satisfied. More generally, see Proposition \ref{prop.e'} below, the global structure of compaclty supported distributions $\mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$ on the group, gives rise to $L^p({\mathbb{G}})$-moderate regularised such nets. We note that following the arguments developed in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop.e'} we can show that the regularised net $(v_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ is $\dot{L}^{2}_{s}({\mathbb{G}})$, and so also $H^{s}({\mathbb{G}})$-moderate for every $s>0$.
head: environment

label: prop.e'
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.e'}
Let $v \in \mathcal{E}^{'}({\mathbb{G}})$, and let 
$v_\epsilon=v*\psi_\epsilon$ be obtained as
the convolution of $v$ with a mollifier $\psi_\epsilon$ as in \eqref{mol}.
Then the regularising net $(v_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ is $L^{p}({\mathbb{G}})$-moderate for any $p \in [1,\infty]$.

label: defn.negl
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn.negl}
{Let $Y$ be a normed space of functions on ${\mathbb{G}}$.
Let $(f_\epsilon)_\epsilon $, $(\tilde{f}_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ be two nets. Then, the net $(f_\epsilon-\tilde{f}_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ is called $Y$-{\em negligible}, if the following condition is satisfied
    \begin{equation}\label{def.cond.negl}
    \|f_\epsilon-\tilde{f}_\epsilon\|_{Y}\lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^k\,,
    \end{equation}
    for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\epsilon \in (0,1]$. In the case where $f_\epsilon=f_\epsilon(t,x)$ is a net depending also on $t \in [0,T]$, then the {\em negligibility condition} \eqref{def.cond.negl} can be regarded as
    \[
    \|f_\epsilon(t,\cdot)-\tilde{f}_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{Y}\lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^k\,,\quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}\,,
    \]
    uniformly in $t \in [0,T]$.} The constant in the inequality \eqref{def.cond.negl} can depend on $k$ but not on $\omega$.

label: th.ex.heat.pos
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Existence of the very weak solution, case $V\geq 0$

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $u_0 \in H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})\cap \mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$. We first treat the case where $V\in L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})\cup \mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$. If $V_\epsilon, u_{o,\epsilon}$ are regularised (via convolution with a Friedrichs' mollifier) nets, then they satisfy the moderateness assumptions of Definition \ref{def.vws.pos}; i.e., we have 
\[
\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb{G}})},\|u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})} \lesssim \epsilon^{-n_0}\,,
\]
where we have chosen $\omega(\epsilon)=\epsilon$, for some $n_0\in \mathbb{N}$. Therefore, using the estimate \eqref{prop.pos.a.claim} we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|u_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})}& \lesssim & (1+\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb{G}})})\|u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})}\\
& \lesssim & \epsilon^{-n_0} \times \epsilon^{-n_0}\\
& = & \epsilon^{-2n_0}\,,
\end{eqnarray*}
uniformly in $t$, and this shows that the net $u_{0,\epsilon}$ is $C([0,T];H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}}))$-moderate, as required. Next we treat the case where $V \in L^{\frac{Q}{\nu}}({\mathbb{G}}) \cap L^{\frac{Q}{2\nu}}({\mathbb{G}})$. Consequently, for the net $V_\epsilon$ as before, the $L^{\frac{Q}{\nu}}({\mathbb{G}}) \cap L^{\frac{Q}{2\nu}}({\mathbb{G}})$-moderateness assumptions for $\omega(\epsilon)=\epsilon$ and for some $n_1 \in \mathbb{N}$ are guaranteed. Thus, using the estimate \eqref{prop.pos.b.claim}, we can write
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|u(t,\cdot)\|_{H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})} & \lesssim & \|u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})}  \left\{\left(1+\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\right) \left(1+\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^{\frac{Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\}\\
& \lesssim & \epsilon^{-n_0} \times \epsilon^{-n_1} \times \epsilon^{-\frac{n_1}{2}}\\
& = & \epsilon^{-n}\,,
\end{eqnarray*}
for some $n$, and the proof of Theorem \ref{th.ex.heat.pos} is complete.
head: environment

label: th.ex.heat.any
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th.ex.heat.any}
Let $V$ be a real function. Let also $u_0 \in L^2({\mathbb{G}}) \cup \mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$ and $V \in L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})\cup \mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$. Then, the very weak solution to the Cauchy problem \eqref{heat.eq} exists.
head: environment
name: Existence of the very weak solution, case $V \in \mathbb{R}$

title: Proof
body_md:
By the assumptions of the theorem, the $L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})$-moderateness assumptions of the net $V_\epsilon$ are satisfied; i.e., for some $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ we have 
\[
\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty ({\mathbb{G}})} \lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^{-n_0}\,.
\]
Taking $\omega$ as $\omega(\epsilon):=(\log \epsilon^{-n_0})^{-\frac{1}{n_0}}$, where $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ is such that the moderateness assumptions can be expressed in the form
\[
\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty ({\mathbb{G}})} \lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^{-n_0}= \log (\epsilon^{-n_0})\,.
\]
For the net $u_{0,\epsilon}$ the $L^2$-moderateness can be simply regarded as
\[
\|u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\lesssim \epsilon^{-n_1}\,, \quad n_1 \in \mathbb{N}\,.
\]
Using the estimate \eqref{prop.neg.a.claim} for the solution to \eqref{heat.eq} in the case of a real potential we deduce that  
\begin{eqnarray*}
  \|u_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}  &\lesssim & \exp(t\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb{G}})})\|u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\\
  & \lesssim & \epsilon^{-tn_0} \times \epsilon^{-n_1}\\
  & \leq & \epsilon^{-Tn_0-n_1}\\
  & = & \epsilon^{-n}\,,
\end{eqnarray*}
for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and this completes the proof of Theorem \ref{th.ex.heat.any}.
head: environment

label: cor.any.sob
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.any.sob}
Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{th.ex.heat.any} the very weak solution $u$ to the Cauchy problem \eqref{heat.eq} is also $H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})$-moderate.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The proof is an immediate consequence of Theorem \ref{th.ex.heat.any} and takes into account Remark \ref{rem.any.sob}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
It is evident that, in the case where $V \geq 0$ and $V_\epsilon$ is a $L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})$-moderate net, one can ease the assumptions on the moderateness of $u_{0,\epsilon}$ as in Definition \ref{def.vws.any} where $V \in \mathbb{R}$ provided the function $\omega(\epsilon)$ as in the moderateness of $V_\epsilon$ is sharp enough; i.e., we require 
\[
\omega(\epsilon)^{-n_1}\leq \log \epsilon^{-n_0}\,,
\]
for some $n_0,n_1 \in \mathbb{N}$. In this case the $C([0,T];L^2({\mathbb{G}}))$-moderateness of $u_\epsilon$ shall be proved using the estimate \eqref{prop.neg.a.claim} that applies to the case of a real potential $V$.

label: rem.negl
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem.negl}
In the work \cite{ARST21c}, Definitions 4,5 and 8 on the uniqueness of the very weak solution to the heat equation in the Euclidean setting considered there, are a less meticulous version of Definitions \ref{defn.uniq.heat.pos} and \ref{defn/uniq.any} that we give here. In particular, the previous and the current definitions differ with respect to the assumptions on the asymptotic behaviour of the nets $V_\epsilon$ and $\tilde{V}_\epsilon$: here we enlarge the requirement that the aforementioned nets approximate $V$ as we simply assume that the difference of nets $V_\epsilon-\tilde{V}_\epsilon$ is $L^\infty$-negligible. In this manner the initial idea to define uniqueness in terms of the stability  of the very weak solution under negligible changes on the coefficient $V$ remains, but we drop the previous requirement for the nets $V_\epsilon$ and $\tilde{V}_\epsilon$ to be regularisations of $V$.

title: Proof
body_md:
If we multiply equation \eqref{heat.eq} by $u$, and integrate over ${\mathbb{G}}$ we derive
\[
	\Re(\langle u_t(t,\cdot),u(t,\cdot)\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{G})}+\langle \mathcal{R}u(t,\cdot),u(t,\cdot)\rangle_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+\langle V(\cdot)u(t,\cdot),u(t,\cdot) \rangle_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})})=0\,,

where the last inequality can be rewritten as

\frac12 \partial_t \|u(t,\cdot)\|{^{2}_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}} = -\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}u(t,\cdot)\|{^{2}_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}}-\|\sqrt{V}(\cdot)u(t,\cdot)\|{^{2}_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}} \leq 0\,,
\]
and the claim \eqref{en.est} follows.

label: thm.un.pos2
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We keep the notation used in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm.un.pos.1} and adapt the reasoning there if necessary. Observe that the next inequality follows by H\"older's inequality combined with the Sobolev embeddings \eqref{inclusions}:
\[
    \|(\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon)(\cdot)\tilde{u}_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \leq \|\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}\tilde{u}_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,,
    \]
    uniformly in $t\in [0,T]$. Now, if in \eqref{mink} we plug in the formula for $f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)$ and the last estimate, then we get 
    \[
    \|U_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \lesssim \|u_{0,\epsilon}-\tilde{u}_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+ \|\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu}}({\mathbb{G}})}\|\tilde{u}_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})}
    \]
    Taking into account the negligiblity and moderateness assumptions we deduce that 
    \[
    \|U_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^{N}\,, \quad \text{for all}\, N \in \mathbb{N}\,,
    \]
    uniformly in $t \in [0,T]$, and for some suitable $\omega(\epsilon)$ and this finishes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm.un.pos2}.

label: thm.un.any
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.un.any}
Let $V\in \mathbb{R}$. Let also $u_0 \in L^2({\mathbb{G}})\cup \mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$ and $V \in L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}})\cup \mathcal{E}'({\mathbb{G}})$. Then, the very weak solution to the Cauchy problem \eqref{heat.eq} is $(L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}}),L^\infty ({\mathbb{G}}))$-unique or $(L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}}), L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu}}({\mathbb{G}}))$-unique, where in the second case we assume that $2Q \geq \nu$.
head: environment

label: EQ:thm.un.3a
title: Proof
body_md:
The arguments developed here follow the same line as in Theorems \ref{thm.un.pos.1} and \ref{thm.un.pos2}. The notation used there is adopted here as well. First we recall the estimate for the solution $U_\epsilon$ yo the Cauhcy problem \eqref{forU1}:
\[
\|U_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\leq \|W_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+\int_{0}^{T}\|\tilde{U}_\epsilon(t-\sigma,\cdot;\sigma)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,d\sigma\,.
\]
Now, the $L^2$-norms appearing on the right-hand side of the above inequality shall be estimated after applying twice the inequality \eqref{prop.neg.a.claim} for the classical solution to \eqref{heat.eq} in the case of a real potential. In particular we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{EQ:thm.un.3a}
  \|U_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\lesssim \|u_{0,\epsilon}-\tilde{u}_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\exp\left(t \|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty ({\mathbb{G}})} \right)+\|f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\exp\left(t \|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty ({\mathbb{G}})} \right)\,.  
\end{equation}
It is necessary for our purposes to consider the $L^\infty$-moderateness of the net $V_\epsilon$ under the choice of the function $\omega$ to be given by $\omega(\epsilon):=\left(\log \epsilon^{-N_0} \right)^{-\frac{1}{N_0}}$, where $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ is such that the moderateness assumption can be expressed as:
\[
\|V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \omega(\epsilon)^{-N_0}=\log (\epsilon^{-N_0})\,,
\]
uniformly in $\epsilon \in (0,1]$.
Let us plug into the estimate \eqref{EQ:thm.un.3a} the moderateness assumption as above and get 
\begin{equation}
    \label{EQ:thm.un.3b}
    \|U_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\lesssim e^{-TN_0} \left[\|u_{0,\epsilon}-\tilde{u}_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+ \|f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\right]\,,
\end{equation}
uniformly in $\epsilon \in (0,1]$. We next need to consider the negligibility of nets involved into \eqref{EQ:thm.un.3b}. First consider the case where the net $\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon$ is $L^\infty$-negligible. Then, using the estimate 
\[
\|f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2} \leq \|\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty} \|\tilde{u}_\epsilon\|_{L^2}\,,
\]
and the $L^2$-moderateness of $\tilde{u}_\epsilon$ as being the very weak solution to \eqref{heat.eq} we get 
\[
\|f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2} \leq \omega(\epsilon)^{-N}\,,
\]
for any $N \in \mathbb{N}$. The latter combined with the $L^2$-negligibility assumption of the net $u_{0,\epsilon}-\tilde{u}_{0,\epsilon}$  under the estimate \eqref{EQ:thm.un.3b} implies the $L^2$-negligiblity of the net $u_\epsilon-\tilde{u}_\epsilon$ and we have shown that the very weak solution to the Cauchy problem \eqref{heat.eq} is $(L^{\infty}({\mathbb{G}}),L^\infty ({\mathbb{G}}))$-unique. Now, for the case where the net $\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon$ is $L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu}}$-negligible, applying H\"older's inequality and using the Sobolev embedding \eqref{inclusions} we get 
\[
   \|f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2} \leq  \|(\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon)(\cdot)\tilde{u}_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \leq \|\tilde{V}_\epsilon-V_\epsilon\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}\tilde{u}_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,.
    \]
    Now, since by Corollary \ref{cor.any.sob} the very weak solution $\tilde{u}_\epsilon$ is $H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}$-moderate, by the last estimate we deduce that the net $f_\epsilon$ is $L^2$-negligible, and consequently also the difference of nets $u_{0,\epsilon}-\tilde{u}_{0,\epsilon}$. The last observations implies that the very weak solution to the problem \eqref{heat.eq} is $(L^\infty,L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu}})$-unique, and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm.un.any} complete.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
We denote by $C_0({\mathbb{G}})$ the space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity; i.e., we write $f \in C_0({\mathbb{G}})$, if for every $\delta>0$ there exists a compact set $K_\delta$ such that 
 \[
 |f|< \delta \quad \text{on}\quad {\mathbb{G}}\setminus K_\delta\,. 
 \]
head: environment
name: Space $C_0(\G)$

label: rem.Linfty
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem.Linfty}
 For a function $f \in C_0({\mathbb{G}})$, we know that for the corresponding regularised net $f_\epsilon$ we have: \[
 \|f_\epsilon\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb{G}})}\leq C<\infty\,,
 \] 
 uniformly in $\epsilon \in (0,1]$.

label: thm.consis.pos.1
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Consistency with the classical solution, case $V \geq 0$

label: eq.m=0
title: Proof
body_md:
For $u$ and for $u_\epsilon$ as in the hypothesis, we introduce the auxiliary notation $W_\epsilon(t,x):=u(t,x)-u_\epsilon(t,x)$. Then, the net $W_\epsilon$ is a solution to the Cauchy problem
	\begin{equation}\label{eq.m=0}
	\begin{cases*}
		\partial_{t}W_\epsilon(t,x)+{\mathcal{R}} W_\epsilon(t,x)+V_\epsilon(x)W_\epsilon(t,x)=f_\epsilon(t,x), \\
		W_\epsilon(0,x)=(u_0-u_{0,\epsilon})(x)\,,
	\end{cases*}
	\end{equation}
	where we denote $f_\epsilon(t,x):=(V_\epsilon(x)-V(x))u(t,x)$.
Analogously to Theorem \ref{thm.un.pos.1}, an application of Duhamel's principle gives:
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{cons.thm1.heat}
 \|W_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} & \lesssim & \|u_{0}-u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+\int_{0}^{T}\|f_\epsilon(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,d\sigma\nonumber\\
 & = & \|u_{0}-u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}+ \int_{0}^{T}\|(V_\epsilon-V)(\cdot)u(t,\cdot)\|\,d \sigma\,,
\end{eqnarray}
 where we have applied Minkowski's integral inequality. 
 
 Let us first consider the case \eqref{itm1}: standard arguments from functional analysis imply that the below $L^p$-norms converge to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$:
\[
\|u_{0}-u_{0,\epsilon}\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,,\|V_\epsilon-V\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\,.
\]
The integrated quantity on the right-hand side of \eqref{cons.thm1.heat} is finite since
\[
\|(V_\epsilon-V)(\cdot)u(t,\cdot)\|\lesssim  \|V_\epsilon-V\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}u(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\,,
\]
as follows by the Sobolev embeddings \eqref{emb},
and consequently, since $u \in H^{\frac{\nu}{2}}({\mathbb{G}})$, we also have the convergence
\[
\|(V_\epsilon-V)(\cdot)u(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \lesssim \|V_\epsilon-V\|_{L^{\frac{2Q}{\nu }}({\mathbb{G}})}\|\sqrt{{\mathcal{R}}}u(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \rightarrow 0\,.
\]
Combining  \eqref{cons.thm1.heat} with the below observations and using Lebesgue's dominated convergence theorem we get 
 \begin{equation}
     \label{duh.e.0}
      \|W_\epsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})} \rightarrow 0\,,
 \end{equation}
 uniformly in $t \in [\sigma,T]$, where $\sigma$ is taken to be fixed. The last conludes the proof of the theorem for the case \eqref{itm1}.
 
 To deal with the case  \eqref{itm2}, inequality on the right-hand side of \eqref{cons.thm1.heat} shall now be estimated as:
 \[
  \|(V_\epsilon-V)(\cdot)u(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2({\mathbb{G}})}\leq \|V_\epsilon-V\|_{L^\infty}\|u(\sigma,\cdot)\|_{L^2}\,.
 \]
 Using Lemmas 3.1.58, 3.1.59 in \cite{FR16} for $V \in C_{0}({\mathbb{G}})$ we have the convergence: $\|V_\epsilon-V\|_{L^\infty}\rightarrow 0$, as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, and the last implies in turn that convergence in \eqref{duh.e.0} is satisfied under the alternative assumptions \eqref{itm2}. Summarising the above, we have shown that the very weak solution converges to the classical one in $L^2$ in both cases \eqref{itm1} and \eqref{itm2}, and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm.consis.pos.1} is complete.
head: environment

label: thm.consis.2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.consis.2}
Let $V$ be a real coefficient, and let $u_0 \in L^2({\mathbb{G}})$. Assume also that  $V \in C_0({\mathbb{G}})$, and also that $V_\epsilon$ is a regularisation of $V$. Then, the regularised net $(u_\epsilon)_\epsilon$ converges, as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, in $L^2({\mathbb{G}})$, to the classical solution $u$ given by Proposition \ref{prop.neg.a}.

title: Proof
head: environment
name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm.consis.2}

label: finrem
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{finrem}
To be consistent with the previous work \cite{ARST21c} on the heat equation on the real case, let us point out that the assumption on the functional space $L^\infty({\mathbb{G}})$ of the coefficient $V$ (denoted by $q$ there) as appears in the consistency results (see Theorems 2.8 and 3.5 in  \cite{ARST21c}) should be restricted to its subspace $C_0({\mathbb{G}})$. Indeed, under such assumptions, the necessary $L^\infty$-convergence of the net $V_\epsilon-V$ is granted, and Theorems 2.8 and 3.5 in \cite{ARST21c} would then follow as a spacial case of Theorem \ref{thm.consis.pos.1} and \ref{thm.consis.2}, respectively, in the particular case where the group ${\mathbb{G}}$ is the trivial one and the Rockland operator is the usual Laplace operator; in symbols, when ${\mathbb{G}}=\mathbb R^d$ and $\mathcal{R}=-\Delta$.
